note: Copy to <destination>/verification/scenarios/corpus.json and edit. This is Operator-approved INTENT: what the source is asked to do, so the destination can be asked exactly the same thing. It records no expected values - those come only from capturing the source (capture-source-scenarios.py).

initial_state.reset: .hermes/skills/gates/capture-source-oracles/scripts/reset-parity-db.sh --root . restores the destination instance; the frozen source restores the same dataset by restarting when its baseline engine is in-memory
initial_state.dataset: the specimen's own seeded dataset, and what is true of it that the scenarios depend on

path_vars.note: values for templated segments of the IDEMPOTENT reads, taken from the source's own seeded data; a read whose path still carries a variable is INCONCLUSIVE, never guessed

scenarios.why: why this scenario is the one that proves the endpoint's behaviour

rules: A concrete URL, never a route pattern: {var} or * refuses. The route stays in the entry-point inventory and is associated with scenario URLs.
Either body_file or body_absent: true. A DELETE legitimately has no body, and that is a fact to record rather than an omission to infer.
A write with no declared effect refuses: an identical response does not prove the write happened.
identity names ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. Credentials are never recorded here.
Prefer a first scenario whose identifier the write does not assign (update a seeded row rather than create one): effect probes are then deterministic on both engines.
One successful response per endpoint is not behavioural coverage. Authentication, rejection and validation failures need scenarios too.
